# Playbook

**Boat names.** The valid boats are Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, and Harbor. There is no "Delta" or any other name. Every claim I file—target, escort, hide coordinate—must use only these names or valid integers. An invalid name wastes the round's opportunity and may carry a penalty. Before I file any escort claim, I check that the name is one of the four.

**Escort claims.** This is the highest-value lever in the game: 5 points per round for a mutual pair, up to 30 points over six rounds versus 4 points from a single hit. Never claim "none." My default is to name the boat I fire at under standing order. Reasoning: that boat was just engaged by me, and a rational player's most natural reciprocal move is to name their attacker back. If I name my target and they name me, we both bank 5. Over the course of the game, watch what the other boats actually name. If I see a boat consistently naming a specific partner, I shift my claim to try to form a mutual pair with that partner instead. The goal is always: find and lock into a mutual pair, then hold it.

**Claims.** When the office tells me the result of my shot, I claim exactly that result. Never bluff a hit on a miss. The trust cost and potential penalty outweigh any short-term gain, and a bluff destroys the coordination foundation that makes escort pairs work.

**Hiding.** Do not hide at cell 5 by default—it is the most obvious first probe. In early rounds, pick an off-center cell. Vary my cell each round so I am not sitting in the same spot while others learn my pattern. If I was hit last round, shift far—ideally to the opposite end of the line or at least 3–4 cells away from where I was. If I was not hit, I can stay put or shift by one or two; staying put is fine if I suspect the shooter has not found me yet. In the final round, do not panic-shift; stay consistent with whatever cell or small neighborhood I have been using.

**Firing.** Follow the standing order: fire at the next live station in the cycle. Do not redirect at Harbor unless I am in a desperate point deficit and willing to accept removal from the board. For the cell I fire at: in the first round I have no information, so I pick a non-center cell (not 5, not a cell I am hiding in). After that, use every piece of information I have. If I hit at cell X in round N, the target was at X and has likely moved; in round N+1 try X±1 or a cell on the opposite side of the line from X. If I have missed several rounds at the same cell, I am not searching—I am repeating. Switch to a different cell each round until I either hit or have eliminated enough cells to narrow it down. Track which cells I have already tried against each target and do not repeat a miss unless I have exhausted other options.

**Notes.** Keep notes short, consistent, and non-revealing. A fixed phrase like "steady on station" is fine. Do not state my hiding cell, my strategy, or my intent to coordinate escorts. Notes are public; any signal I send can be read by all three opponents and Harbor.

**End-game adjustment.** In the final round, do not change my hiding cell as a last-minute panic move. Do not take extra risks on claims or targets unless the point swing is guaranteed. The escort claim in the final round is just as valuable as in any other round—make it count by naming a boat I have reason to believe will name me back.

# Playbook

**Firing:**
When the standing order tells me who to fire at, I commit to that target for the entire game. I start on a cell and if I get a hit, I keep firing that same cell until I miss twice in a row. If I miss three rounds in a row at a cell, I rotate to a different cell — pick one that is not a round number (1, 5, 9) and not adjacent to my previous fire cell. Never change my fire cell on a whim or because it's the "final round." The point is persistence with a fallback: lock in a cell, give it three rounds, then move if it's clearly wrong.

**Hiding:**
When I hide, I pick a cell that is not a round number (1, 5, 9) and keep it for at least 3 rounds. If I get hit, I move immediately to a cell that is NOT adjacent to my previous cell and NOT a round number. Vary deliberately, not randomly. In this game my hiding worked well — I was hit at most once across six rounds — so I keep this approach.

**Escort claims:**
This is where I lost the most. I name the boat I fire at — the one the standing order puts in front of me. I name that same boat every single round. A mutual escort is worth 5 points per round, 30 over a full game. If the other boat is playing rationally, they will also name me since I am their consistent target. If they don't reciprocate within two rounds, I switch to naming the boat that fires at me instead, and commit to that.

**CRITICAL: I may only name boats that actually exist in this game.** I read the boat list at the start of the episode and I keep it in mind. If the boats are Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, and Harbor, those are the only four names I ever put in an escort claim. Naming a boat that is not on the board is an invalid claim and scores zero. I check before I write.

**Notes:**
I keep my note short, calm, and consistent — "steady on station" or similar. I do not signal intention to move, I do not signal my hide cell, and I do not deviate from the pattern I established in round 1. Consistency reads as trust, and trust is what gets me that mutual escort.

**Claims:**
I always file the claim that matches the private result I was told. No exceptions. The penalty for a false claim outweighs any marginal gain from bluffing.

**Harbor:**
I never fire at Harbor. The standing order never tells me to, and the jettison mechanism is not worth the "off the board" threat. I stay on the cycle.

**What went wrong last game:**
- I named "Delta" and "Golf" as escort claims. Those boats do not exist in this game. Every escort claim I filed was invalid and scored zero. The strategy was right; the execution was a disaster. I must always cross-check my escort name against the actual boat list.
- I fired at cell 5 all six rounds and never hit. I needed a rotation rule after three misses, which I now have.
- My hiding and note strategy worked fine. I keep those exactly as they are.

# Playbook

**Hiding**
- Never hide at 5. It is the "default" center and opponents converge on it.
- Alternate between a small set of off-center cells (e.g., 2, 7, 3, 8) so I do not establish a single predictable spot.
- If an opponent has hit me twice in a row, they have found my pattern; jump to a cell far from my last position.
- In the final round, prioritize survival: pick a cell far from where my attacker has recently fired and far from my previous position.

**Firing**
- Follow the standing order for the target in every round except when the Harbor exception below applies.
- The fire value is the cell I am shooting at, so I am guessing the target's hidden cell. Vary my guesses across rounds rather than repeating the same number.
- Track which cells have produced hits or misses against each target. If a target has been hit at a particular cell, they may return there; if a cell has produced repeated misses, the target is likely elsewhere. Weight my next guess toward cells that are off-center and not recently tried.
- **Harbor exception:** If it is the final round and I am ahead by 3+ points, fire at Harbor instead of my standing-order target. The 3-point transfer is guaranteed ("landed or not") and the "off the board" threat is meaningless with no rounds remaining. This is pure +3 with zero downside.

**Claims**
- Always claim exactly what the office told me. A false claim costs more points than the hit itself is worth. The office knows the truth; there is no bluffing benefit.

**Escort claims**
- Never say "none." This forfeits the only free-points mechanism in the game.
- **Only name boats that actually exist in this picket.** In a 4-station game the valid names are the three other boats plus Harbor. Naming a nonexistent boat earns nothing and wastes the slot.
- Pick one real partner boat and name them every round. Consistency gives them the clearest signal to name me back, and each mutual pair is worth 5 points per round.
- Which boat to pick: name the boat that is firing at you (your standing-order attacker). They are most "engaged" with you and most likely to reciprocate. If I observe a boat naming me before I have named them, switch to naming them immediately to lock in the mutual pair.
- If no one has named me after two rounds, switch to the other candidate boat in round 3 to test whether they will reciprocate.

**Notes**
- Keep notes short. They have no mechanical effect but a distinct note avoids signaling coordination. A brief variation from the group's uniform phrasing is sufficient; do not overthink it.

**General**
- The biggest point source I can control is the escort mutual pair (5 per round × up to 6 rounds = up to 30 points). Prioritize establishing and maintaining it above all other tactical considerations.
- In the final round, weigh: (1) safety of my hide cell, (2) whether the Harbor exception applies, (3) keeping my escort claim consistent. Do all three in the same round if possible.
